- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >40), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >35, consider 3–5 day decay toward historical mean (avg of last 10–15 days).
- Sentiment history is flat (0.00) across all examples — no signal to adjust for sentiment; treat as neutral baseline.
- Forecast error is most severe in the first 10 days of the 30-day window; apply stronger correction for early days (e.g., reduce by 2–3% per day until day 7).
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after spike (e.g., 44 → 31), model often fails to anticipate; add a 3–5 day lag correction to prevent premature recovery.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days are high, forecast should not exceed 10% above the 30-day moving average.
